definitions:
(these are the ones the dashboard and docs quote):
  core decision      = outcome label + amount (±$0.01) + escalation flag; account flags and citations are NOT part of it
  model escalated    = the arm's own ruling already said "escalate" (goes to a human regardless of any gate)
  blocked by gate    = the certificate/verifier turned a non-escalated ruling into human review
  human flow         = model escalated + blocked by gate   (what an ops team would actually receive)
  auto               = cleared for automatic execution of the core action
  wrong & executed   = auto AND core decision wrong — the number that matters
caveat_raw: the raw arm is given the case JSON without fact ids, so the verifier's citation rule blocks every raw ruling that is not an escalation; the raw+gate row shows an interface requirement, not the gate's discriminative power

human_reasons: safety concern confirmed (F11, F10, F4); segment finding undetermined for F11; evidence gap: No prior chat history or call logs between rider and driver are in the record; only the 3-message thread (F12) is available, so whether the threat was isolated or part of a pattern must be checked by the human reviewer.

Safety-typed dispute with an alleged threat/intimidation in the in-ride chat: rider asked to get out at 17:19 [F3], driver replied at 17:20 "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], rider complains she felt unsafe for the whole ride [case complaint], driver's after-the-fact statement offers a safety justification [F6]. Complete timestamped chat [F5]. Human reviewer to read the thread in context and decide code-of-conduct / account action under SAFE-1; check whether any injury or dangerous-driving element arises under SAFE-2 (995 / commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP). No fare issue: fixed RydeX fare, actual 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km [F1], so nothing refundable and no amount proposed.

Confirmed threat of physical violence in the chat record: rider's 18:22 message “Say that again and I will punch you.” [F4] in reply to the driver's no-smoking request at 18:21 [F3], matching the driver's safety complaint [F6]. Substantive route/overcharge questions are moot — the metered trip was 8.8 km actual vs 8.9 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -1%) [F1] over 13.3 min vs 16 min estimated [F2], so no off-route segment exists and no fare adjustment arises.

Rider filed a safety dispute alleging speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder, and that she felt scared; a dangerous-driving allegation requires human review and cannot be settled on this record, which holds no driving telemetry and no relevant chat content [F6][F3][F4][F5][F1][F2][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Rider complaint of harassment and an unwanted request for her number during the trip (safety dispute; SAFE-1). The in-app chat is empty [F3] and the only driver account is a post-trip denial that does not address the specific allegation [F4], so the record cannot settle what was said. No automatic ruling is permitted on a safety incident; a human reviewer must take a statement from both parties and decide, with the rider informed of the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP paths if the allegation is confirmed [SAFE-2].

Rider filed a safety incident alleging speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder during a RydeX trip NUS → Raffles Place (pickup 08:36, drop-off 08:52), saying she was scared and felt unsafe. The system trace gives no driving-behaviour evidence: distance and duration match the estimate (10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal, 16.1 min vs 16 min) [F1][F2], and the chat holds only the pickup arrangement messages [F3][F4][F5], so the manner of driving cannot be corroborated or refuted from the record. Human review should also note the driver's post-trip statement calling the rider "stupid", which is abuse aimed at the other party under SAFE-1 [F6]. Check: any in-app or telematics/gyro-acceleration data, other rider/driver reports in the same time window [F8 profile shows no prior disputes], and whether the complaint was filed within the NS-7 30-day window. Report paths: 995 if medical assistance is needed, driver's commercial motor insurance for a medical claim, RydeHELP for the safety report [SAFE-2].

safety concern suspected (F8, F7, F3); evidence gap: No evidence gap on the routing: F3's segment and the F6 fare are measured and settled. What the reviewer needs to assess is non-quantitative — the effect of Chat #2 [F8] on the rider in context [F7], and whether any RD-4 justification exists contrary to F11–F14.

safety concern confirmed (F11, F12); evidence gap: None material: chat record complete and timestamped (F12), GPS/timeline consistent (F2, F5, F6). The only open point is whether a 42 m stationary position satisfies "at the pick-up location" under NS-1(ii) — Ryde has published no radius (G2).

Safety dispute with a suspected SAFE-1 conduct issue (possible confinement threat at F4, in response to the rider's request to exit at F3), and the record lacks the audio/telematics needed to settle meaning or context; escalating for human review with no fare remedy (no off-route segment: 15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal [F1]) and no account flag (RD-6 'repeated' condition not met on [F8]).

Safety incident: the rider's message at 18:22, "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4], is an express threat of physical violence toward the driver, sent one minute after the driver's lawful request not to smoke in the car [F3], and it is preserved in a complete, fully timestamped two-message chat record [F5]. The driver separately reports the same threat in writing after the trip [F6]. Per SAFE-1 no automated ruling is made; the file goes to a human reviewer with this summary. For the reviewer's benefit the non-safety facts are clean and need no adjustment: the metered RydeTAXI fare of $21.26 corresponds to a route whose actual distance 8.8 km is 0.1 km shorter than the optimal 8.9 km [F1], over 13.3 min against a 16 min estimate [F2], so no unexempted off-route segment exists and the RD-1/RD-2 recoverable amount is zero; nothing in the driving record supports a dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-2 is not raised against the driver [F1][F2]. The parties' profiles — rider 3.6-year account, rating 4.5, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days [F7]; driver 2.0 years, rating 4.85, 427 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld [F8] — are context only and decide nothing [SAFE-1]. The only open question for the reviewer is what consequence, if any, attaches to the threat [F4].

Rider alleges dangerous driving (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) on trip Jurong East MRT → NUS, 21:22–21:34, fare $21.04 fixed; SAFE-2 requires a human reviewer. Record contains no measurement of speed, braking or shoulder use: GPS shows only distance and time [F1][F2]; the complete, fully timestamped 2-message chat is pickup logistics only [F3][F4][F5]; the driver's post-trip statement denies any complaint was made [F6]; both profiles show 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d [F7][F8]. Disputed: the manner of driving, which only the rider's complaint and the driver's denial speak to.

Rider-filed harassment/safety complaint (body comments, request for her number, stated feeling of harassment and unsafety) — SAFE-1 requires human review and no automatic ruling; the record is a word-against-word dispute with no in-app chat (F3) and only the driver's post-trip denial (F4), so the content of the spoken exchange cannot be settled from the file.

Safety ticket under SAFE-2: rider alleges speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking over the 08:36–08:52 NUS→Raffles Place trip, and the driver's post-trip statement uses insulting language ("rider is stupid") toward her, a SAFE-1 abuse issue. No telematics, speed-band or traffic facts exist for the actual route, so the driving allegation is neither corroborated nor refuted; F1/F2 (10.6 km vs 10.7 km; 16.1 min vs 16 min) rule out only route deviation and excess mileage [F1][F2]. Chat is complete and timestamped but contains only pickup logistics and no in-trip safety report [F3][F4][F5]. Fixed $24.76 RydeX fare, no fare/add-on facts, and no refund is claimed, so no amount is computed [F1][FARE-1]. Reviewer should check: any telematics or speed-band record for the actual line, the driver's demeanour/statement [F6], and weigh the absence of an in-trip objection against a complaint first made after drop-off; note 995 / driver commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting routes to the rider.
